checks: Exactly three described tools advertise typed input and output schemas.
Data lookup succeeds without a persistence side effect.
Each tool exposes a clear is_error failure; failed lookup/orchestration writes nothing.
Action persists a task, deduplicates identical retries, and rejects conflicting retries.
Orchestration combines the lookup result with a persisted task.
Data lookup also leaves an existing database unchanged.
Tasks survive a fresh server process; retries leave exactly two database rows.

tools.name: find_study_resource
tools.title: Find a study resource
tools.description:
DATA: Retrieve one learning resource from the fictional, bundled campus catalog.

Use for information-only requests. Returns the resource title, sample campus
location, summary and focus points. Matching is exact against a canonical
topic or its documented aliases, ignoring case/whitespace. Does not touch
task storage. Unknown topics produce an error listing available topics.

topic.description: Topic or alias: Python async (python, asyncio), REST APIs (rest, http), or MCP tools (mcp). Case and whitespace are ignored.

outputSchema.description: One record from the bundled, explicitly fictional demonstration catalog.

resource_id.description: Stable identifier in the sample catalog.

title.description: Title to use when creating a study task.

summary.description: What this sample learning resource covers.

location.description: Fictional campus location, not a real reservation or URL.

is_sample.description: Always true: this is fictional sample data.

tools.name: create_study_task
tools.title: Create a study task
tools.description:
ACTION: Save one study intention to local, durable SQLite task storage.

Use when the user asks to save a task for a known resource title. Returns
its persisted identifier, title, duration, status, request key and original
UTC creation time. This does not schedule a calendar event or reserve a
resource. Identical request_id/payload retries return the original task;
reusing a key with a different title or duration is an explicit error.

resource_title.description: Title of the resource to study; use the exact lookup result title when available.

minutes.description: Study duration as a whole number of minutes, from 5 through 180.

request_id.description: Caller-chosen unique key for this intended task. Reuse the same key and payload for retries; use a fresh key for a new task.

outputSchema.description: A durably saved study intention; it is not a calendar appointment.

task_id.description: Unique identifier generated once and persisted.

minutes.description: Planned study duration in whole minutes.

request_id.description: Idempotency key supplied by the caller.

status.description: New tasks are planned, not completed.

created_at.description: Original creation timestamp in UTC ISO 8601 format.

tools.name: plan_study_session
tools.title: Plan a study session
tools.description:
ORCHESTRATION: Look up a topic, then save a task for the selected resource.

Use for a higher-level request to find a suitable resource and save a study
intention. Calls the same data operation followed by the same action
operation; returns both typed results. Invalid input or unknown topic causes
no task write. Identical retries reuse the saved task; conflicting request
keys fail clearly. Never call create_study_task again after this succeeds.

topic.description: Topic or alias: Python async (python, asyncio), REST APIs (rest, http), or MCP tools (mcp). Case and whitespace are ignored.

minutes.description: Study duration as a whole number of minutes, from 5 through 180.

request_id.description: Caller-chosen unique key for this intended task. Reuse the same key and payload for retries; use a fresh key for a new task.

outputSchema.description: The lookup result together with the task saved for that exact resource.
